title: Why Do Volcanoes Erupt? It's Not What You Think
description:
Volcanoes do not erupt just because they fill up. Rising magma loses pressure, dissolved gas bubbles out and expands, and the blast cracks the rock open. Here is the whole chain in under a minute.

#volcano #science #geology #shorts #earthscience

beats.sentence: Deep underground, rock melts into glowing magma.
beats.subject: volcano

beats.sentence: Magma is lighter than the rock around it, so it rises and pools in a chamber.
beats.subject: volcano
beats.change: the glow climbs brighter as magma rises

beats.sentence: As more magma flows in, the chamber swells and the pressure climbs.
beats.subject: volcano

beats.sentence: Inside the magma, dissolved gas is packed tight.

beats.sentence: As the magma rises, the pressure drops and the gas bubbles out, spreading wider and wider.
beats.subject: particles

beats.sentence: Those bubbles expand and speed up, shoving the magma upward.
beats.subject: particles

beats.sentence: When the pressure beats the strength of the rock above, the cone cracks open.
beats.subject: volcano
beats.change: the crater bursts into a growing eruption

beats.sentence: Magma blasts out of the vent, glowing at about one thousand degrees Celsius.
beats.subject: volcano
beats.change: the eruption grows to full blast

beats.sentence: It is like a pressure cooker, where the needle climbs until the lid gives way.

beats.sentence: Eruptions throw up ash that can cool the planet for a year or two.

beats.sentence: Early volcanic gas probably helped build Earth's air and oceans.
